rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence resumes the Moses–Pharaoh narrative and introduces the ensuing dialogue; it may coordinate with 20:49 after an ellipsis or stand parenthetically.
rows.anchor: قصص موسى عليه السلام مع فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath lām and qad express amazement at Pharaoh’s tenacity and stress how firmly he persisted in disbelief despite Moses’ many signs.
rows.anchor: وتأكيد الكلام بلام القسم و ( قد ) مستعمل في التعجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are summarized and generalized here to emphasize Pharaoh’s resistance, unlike al-Aʿrāf, where the aim is to show their succession and support.
rows.anchor: وأجملت وعممت فلم تفصل ، لأن المقصود هنا بيان شدة تصلبه في كفره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s showing Pharaoh the signs means making them manifest so that he witnessed them.
rows.anchor: وإراءة الله إياه الآيات : إظهارها له بحيث شاهدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive identifies the familiar signs performed through Moses: the staff, white hand, famine years, locusts, lice, frogs, blood, flood, and the sea’s parting.
rows.anchor: وهي المذكورة في قوله تعالى : { في تسع آيات إلى فرعون وقومه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh continued denying after all the signs, even entering the parted sea in hope of capturing the Israelites.
rows.anchor: وقد استمر تكذيبه بعد جميعها حتى لما رأى انفلاق البحر اقتحمه طمعا للظفر ببني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic kullah intensifies the audience’s wonder at Pharaoh’s stubbornness; a similar totalizing emphasis appears in the account of Pharaoh’s people.
rows.anchor: وتأكيد الآيات بأداة التوكيد { كلها } لزيادة التعجيب من عناده

rows.speaker: المفسرين
rows.claim: Commentators commonly coordinate 20:56 with 20:49 and make 20:49 explain the denial; this wrongly suggests all signs preceded Pharaoh’s summoning magicians, though many came much later. The waw does not require sequence.
rows.anchor: وظاهر صنيع المفسرين أنهم جعلوا جملة ولقد أريناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce talqaf with fatḥa on lām and a doubled qāf; Ḥafṣ reads it with a still lām and an ungeminated qāf, from laqifa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور تلقف بفتح اللام وتشديد القاف .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In innamā, mā is relative; kaydu sāḥir is the predicate, so the sentence simply reports what they did rather than restricting it. The written connection does not reflect the distinction earlier scribes observed.
rows.anchor: و { كيد ساحر } خبر ( إن ) . والكلام إخبار بسيط لا قصر فيه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read sāḥir with an alif after sīn; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read siḥr with kasra on sīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { كيد ساحر بألف بعد السين . وقرأه حمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف كيد سحر بكسر السين .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause continues the previous sentence and is circumstantial of its pronoun: magic fails because sustained reflection and composure expose it.
rows.anchor: فهي معطوفة عليها وحال من ضمير { إنما صنعوا } ، أي لا ينجح الساحر حيث كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite noun denotes the generic, familiar class: no sorcerer succeeds by sorcery.
rows.anchor: وتعريف { الساحر تعريف الجنس لقصد الجنس المعروف ، أي لا يفلح بها كل ساحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Atā was chosen instead of kāna or ḥalla because most magicians had been brought from across Egypt, and because it preserves the verse endings.
rows.anchor: واختير فعل أتى } دون نحو : حيث كان ، أو حيث حل ، لمراعاة كون معظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase generalizes over every place the sorcerer attends with his magic.
rows.anchor: وتعميم { حيث أتى } لعموم الأمكنة التي يحضرها ، أي بسحره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial concerns success in sorcery, not a sorcerer’s trade or other affairs; the generic negative also universalizes the relevant acts and places.
rows.anchor: وتعليق الحكم بوصف الساحر يقتضي أن نفي الفلاح عن الساحر في أمور السحر لا في تجارة أو غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening fa coordinates with an omitted clause: Moses threw, the staff swallowed their work, as in the command to strike the sea and its parting.
rows.anchor: الفاء عاطفة على محذوف يدل عليه قوله { وألق ما في يمينك } ( طه : 69 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive means they cast themselves down, since nobody else cast them; their prostration publicly acknowledged Moses as God’s messenger.
rows.anchor: وأسند الفعل إلى المجهول لأنهم لا ملقي لهم إلا أنفسهم ، فكأنه قيل : فألقوا أنفسهم سجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible sense is that the magicians prostrated in worship of God.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون سجودهم تعظيما لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that they prostrated to honor Moses after recognizing his victory over them.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون دلالة على تغلب موسى عليهم فسجدوا تعظيما له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may instead have honored Pharaoh as a precaution against his violence before declaring faith.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يريدوا به تعظيم فرعون ، جعلوه مقدمة لقولهم { ءامنا برب هارون وموسى } حذرا من بطشه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sujjad is the plural of sājid.
rows.anchor: وسجد : جمع ساجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qālū may be a circumstantial clause, an appositional specification of what their prostration contained, or an independent opening of dialogue.
rows.anchor: وجملة { قالوا } يصح أن تكون في موضع الحال ، أي ألقوا قائلين .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They believed at that moment because, as masters of sorcery, they knew Moses’ feat was not magic but a sign from God.
rows.anchor: وإنما آمنوا بالله حينئذ لأنهم أيقنوا أن ما جرى على يد موسى ليس من جنس السحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They identified God by relation to Moses and Aaron because those were the names by which they knew him, among people who worshipped other gods, including Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: وتعبيرهم عن الرب بطريق الإضافة إلى هارون وموسى لأن الله لم يكن يعرف بينهم يومئذ إلا بهذه النسبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting Aaron before Moses here and Moses before Aaron in al-Aʿrāf implies no rank: the coordinating waw conveys only their joint inclusion.
rows.anchor: لا دلالة فيه على تفضيل ولا غيره ، لأن الواو العاطفة لا تفيد أكثر من مطلق الجمع في الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿrāf also reports their confession as belief in the Lord of all worlds; this account omits that wording because reports need not reproduce everything, only what serves the context.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى أنه حكي في سورة الأعراف ( 121 ) قول السحرة { قالوا آمنا برب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron’s precedence here may be the narrator’s choice for the rhyme, rather than the order in the magicians’ original speech; another report places Moses first.
rows.anchor: ووجه تقديم هارون هنا الرعاية على الفاصلة ، فالتقديم وقع في الحكاية لا في المحكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the magicians may have uttered both formulas, naming Aaron first for seniority and Moses first for his greater prophetic rank and divine speech.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تقديم هارون في هذه الآية من حكاية قول السحرة ، فيكون صدر منهم قولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āmana lahu means faith arose for his sake, while āmana bihi means faith arose because of him; the verb normally takes a preposition in this sense.
rows.anchor: ويقال : آمن له ، أي حصل عنده الإيمان لأجله . كما يقال : آمن به ، أي حصل الإيمان عنده بسببه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qālūn, Warsh by al-Azraq, Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū ʿAmr, Abū Jaʿfar, and Rawḥ read with one hamza and lengthening, as an interrogative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قالون وورش من طريق الأزرق ، وابن عامر ، وأبو عمرو ، وأبو جعفر ، وروح عن يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warsh by al-Aṣbahānī, Ibn Kathīr, Ḥafṣ, and Ruways read with one hamza as a declarative rebuke.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ورش من طريق الأصفهاني ، وابن كثير ، وحفص عن عاصم ، ورويس عن يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Abū Bakr, and Khalaf read with two hamzas, also interrogatively.
rows.anchor: وقرأه حمزة ، والكسائي ، وأبو بكر عن عاصم ، وخلف بهمزتين على الاستفهام أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unable to punish belief without violating debate conventions, Pharaoh invented the charge that they believed before receiving his permission and treated it as insolence.
rows.anchor: ولكنه علم أن العقاب على الإيمان بموسى بعد أن فتح باب المناظرة معه نكث لأصول المناظرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh pretended their haste proved prior collusion with Moses and claimed he would have permitted belief, to make the audience doubt what they had witnessed.
rows.anchor: واستخلص من تسرعهم بذلك أنهم تواطؤوا مع موسى من قبل فأظهروا العجز عند مناظرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the familiar defeated person’s feeble invented excuse, like defendants accusing judges of bribery or losing states alleging military treason.
rows.anchor: وهذه شنشنة من قديم الزمان اختلاق المغلوب بارد العذر . ومن هذا القبيل اتهام المحكوم عليهم الحاكمين بالارتشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both pronouns refer to Moses.
rows.anchor: وضمير له } عائد إلى موسى مثل ضمير { إنه لكبيركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before I permit you means before I allow you to believe in him; adhina lahu means to authorize something.
rows.anchor: ومعنى قبل أن آذن لكم } قبل أن أسوغ لكم أن تؤمنوا به . يقال : أذن له ، إذ أباح له شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqṭīʿ intensifies cutting, with emphasis on the manner: the hand and foot are cut from opposite sides, alternating the limbs.
rows.anchor: والتقطيع : شدة القطع . ومرجع المبالغة إلى الكيفية ، وهي ما وصفه بقوله { من خلاف }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crosswise cutting was apparently the customary mark of criminals; the verse reports the practice rather than distinguishing a uniquely more painful form.
rows.anchor: والظاهر : أن القطع على هذه الكيفية كان شعارا لقطع المجرمين ، فيكون ذكر هذه الصفة حكاية للواقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islamic punishment for ḥirābah cuts only one limb for each offense, mercifully preserving use of the remaining limbs.
rows.anchor: وأما ما جاء في الإسلام في عقوبة المحارب فإنما هو قطع عضو واحد عند كل حرابة فهو من الرحمة في العقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min marks the starting point: cutting begins from opposite sides; the phrase is circumstantial.
rows.anchor: و ( من ) في قوله { من خلاف } للابتداء ، أي يبدأ القطع من مبدأ المخالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taṣlīb intensifies crucifixion, which means binding a body to an upright piece of wood or nailing it there; the emphasis is on forceful nailing.
rows.anchor: والتصليب : مبالغة في الصلب . والصلب : ربط الجسم على عود منتصب أو دقه عليه بمسامير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition fī replaces ʿalā to portray the crucified as firmly embedded in the trunk, using a container metaphor.
rows.anchor: ولذلك عدل عن حرف الاستعلاء إلى حرف الظرفية تشبيها لشدة تمكن المصلوب من الجذع بتمكن الشيء الواقع في وعائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judhūʿ is the plural of judhʿ, a palm-tree trunk.
rows.anchor: والجذوع : جمع جذع بكسر الجيم وسكون الذال وهو عود النخلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayyunā asks which of two participants has the harsher punishment; taʿlamunna is suspended from taking an object because the question follows.
rows.anchor: استفهام عن مشتركين في شدة التعذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh means himself and Moses’ Lord: he boasts that his punishment exceeds the torment Moses warned them of, an expression of arrogance.
rows.anchor: وأراد بالمشتركين نفسه ورب موسى سبحانه لأنه علم من قولهم آمنا برب هارون وموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers’ reply confirms the comparison: God is better than Pharaoh, and His reward and punishment outlast Pharaoh’s favor and threat.
rows.anchor: ويدل على أن ذلك مراد فرعون ما قابل به المؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding patience with what they say, God forbids marveling at the disbelievers’ wealth and children; their worldly provision serves divine purposes, including establishing proof against them.
rows.anchor: أعقب أمره بالصبر على ما يقولونه بنهيه عن الإعجاب بما ينعم به من تنعم من المشركين بأموال وبنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azwāj here evokes families and households: the provision enjoyed by people and their spouses includes each partner’s beauty and shared goods such as children, furnishings, and homes.
rows.anchor: وذكر الأزواج هنا لدلالته على العائلات والبيوت ، أي إلى ما متعناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Extending the eyes means looking for a long time in amazement, not admiration, like extending a hand toward something desired.
rows.anchor: ومد العينين : مستعمل في إطالة النظر للتعجيب لا للإعجاب ، شبه ذلك بمد اليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zahrah, with fatḥa on zāʾ and a still hāʾ, is a flower or plant blossom; figuratively it is the dazzling adornment of worldly life.
rows.anchor: والزهرة بفتح الزاي وسكون الهاء : واحدة الزهر ، وهو نور الشجر والنباتت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly adornment includes clothing, livestock, gardens, women, and children, as in the verse about worldly enjoyment and its adornment.
rows.anchor: فزهرة الحياة : زينة الحياة ، أي زينة أمور الحياة من اللباس والأنعام والجنان والنساء والبنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zahrata al-ḥayāh al-dunyā is an accusative circumstantial phrase describing the relative pronoun in mā.
rows.anchor: على الحال من اسم الموصول في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce zahrah with a still hāʾ; Yaʿqūb reads the hāʾ with fatḥa, a dialectal form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور زهرة بسكون الهاء . وقرأه يعقوب بفتح الهاء وهي لغة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Li-naftinahum attaches to mattaʿnā, and fī expresses figurative containment: each kind of provision carries a fitting trial.
rows.anchor: لنفتنهم } متعلق ب { متعنا } . و ( في ) للظرفية المجازية ، أي ليحصل فتنتهم في خلاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām marks figurative consequence rather than actual motive, as in Pharaoh’s household taking Moses in so he would become their enemy and grief.
rows.anchor: واللام للعلة المجازية التي هي عاقبة الشيء ، مثل قوله تعالى : { فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many interrelated features of social organization lead God to grant worldly adornment; its actual outcome is a trial in their faith, treated as though it were the motive.
rows.anchor: وإنما متعهم الله بزهرة الدنيا لأسباب كثيرة متسلسلة عن نظم الاجتماع فكانت لهم فتنة في دينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitnah is disturbance and mental turmoil from fear, anticipation, or confused affairs; shirk brings disbelievers gloom and apprehension, and their afterlife trial is evident.
rows.anchor: والفتنة : اضطراب النفس وتبلبل البال من خوف أو توقع أو التواء الأمور ، وكانوا لا يخلون من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī is used for figurative containment, illustrated by Sabrah ibn ʿAmr al-Faqʿasī’s verse and the command to provide and clothe dependents therein.
rows.anchor: في قول سبرة بن عمرو الفقعسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concluding statement explains that believers’ God-given provision is better and more lasting than disbelievers’ attractive but inwardly troubled life, and its benefit endures through gratitude.
rows.anchor: إلى آخره يفيد أن ما يبدو للناظر من حسن شارتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive phrase honors the provision: although all sustenance comes from God, disbelievers’ provision is treated as detached because it is mixed with anger and ingratitude’s consequences.
rows.anchor: فإضافة { رزق ربك } إضافة تشريف ، وإلا فإن الرزق كله من الله ، ولكن رزق الكافرين لما خالطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr is a relative comparison across dimensions: some goods benefit now but harm later, some mix benefits with trials, and some fit strongly or weakly; here it favors safety from harms and trials.
rows.anchor: و { خير } تفضيل ، والخيرية حقيقة اعتبارية تختلف باختلاف نواحيها . فمنها : خير لصاحبه في العاجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahl answers the preceding mention of spouses: the Prophet and his family are to find their enjoyment in prayer rather than worldly decoration; a man’s family is his most exemplary dependents.
rows.anchor: ذكر الأهل هنا مقابل لذكر الأزواج في قوله { إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم } ( طه : 131 )

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari reports that Fatima sought a captive servant because grinding exhausted her; the Prophet told her and Ali that tasbih, tahmid, and takbir, each thirty-three times after prayer, was better than a servant.
rows.anchor: فأخبرت عائشة بذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فجاءها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد أخذت وعلي مضجعهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands the Messenger to persevere in prayer even more than he commands his family; iṣṭibār means restraint and figuratively means abundant voluntary prayer.
rows.anchor: وأمر الله رسوله بما هو أعظم مما يأمر به أهله وهو أن يصطبر على الصلاة . والاصطبار : الانحباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is parenthetical between the command and the assurance that God provides.
rows.anchor: وجملة { لا نسألك رزقا } معترضة بين التي قبلها وبين جملة { نحن نرزقك } جعلت تمهيدا لهاته الأخيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God requires worship alone, as gratitude for His favor, not payment; this refutes the taxes and tribute people customarily pay rulers and tribal or military leaders.
rows.anchor: أي ما كلفناك إلا بالعبادة ، لأن العبادة شكر لله على ما تفضل به على الخلق ولا يطلب الله منهم جزاء آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s assurance that He provides explains the preceding verse’s promise that the Lord’s provision is better and lasting: that provision is directed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فجملة { نحن نرزقك } مبينة لجملة { ورزق ربك خير وأبقى } ( طه : 131 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address first concerns the Prophet, but includes his household and believers because the reason for the command applies to all Muslims.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من هذا الخطاب ابتداء هو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ويشمل أهله والمؤمنين لأن المعلل به هذه الجملة مشترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement is coordinated with God’s not asking for provision and explains perseverance in prayer: what is required is piety, whose end is good.
rows.anchor: وجملة { والعاقبة للتقوى } عطف على جملة { لا نسألك رزقا } المعلل بها أمره بالاصطبار للصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀqibah is whatever follows an affair, good or bad, though common usage favors a good outcome; piety ultimately yields good outcomes.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة العاقبة : أنها كل ما يعقب أمرا ويقع في آخره من خير وشر ، إلا أنها غلب استعمالها في أمور الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām marks possession and confirms the intended good outcome; this holds absolutely for the hereafter and may also hold for worldly good.
rows.anchor: واللام للملك تحقيقا لإرادة الخير من العاقبة لأن شأن لام الملك أن تدل على نوال الأمر المرغوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a universal coda, the sentence means that the outcome belongs only to the pious and has the force of a proverb.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة تذييل لما فيها من معنى العموم ، أي لا تكون العاقبة إلا للتقوى . فهذه الجملة أرسلت مجرى المثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min after the negation is extra and strengthens it.
rows.anchor: من رسول } مزيد لتوكيد النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to worship God follows from the declaration that no deity exists besides Him; worship is therefore His alone.
rows.anchor: وفرع فيما أوحي إليهم أمره إياهم بعبادته على الإعلان بأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read yūḥā with a passive third-person verb; Ḥafṣ, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read it actively in the first-person plural, nuḥī.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { إلا يوحى إليه بمثناة تحتية مبنيا للنائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exceptive construction is a disjunctive exception functioning circumstantially.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { إلا يوحى إليه بمثناة تحتية مبنيا للنائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After refuting their worship of other gods, the passage turns to another false belief: that God took a child.
rows.anchor: عطف قصة من أقوالهم الباطلة على قصة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khuzāʿah on Mecca’s outskirts claimed angels were God’s daughters by noble jinn; some Quraysh and other Arabs shared the claim.
rows.anchor: وقد كانت خزاعة من سكان ضواحي مكة يزعمون أن الملائكة بنات الله من سروات الجن وشاركهم في هذا الزعم بعض من قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walad is a collective noun with the same form for singular and plural, includes sons and daughters, and here refers to daughters.
rows.anchor: والولد اسم جمع مفرده مثله ، أي اتخذ أولادا ، والولد يشمل الذكر والأنثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking a child would imply need and deficiency in the Necessary Existent; God is far above that because such need arises from lacking a child.
rows.anchor: ولما كان اتخاذ الولد نقصا في جانب واجب الوجود أعقب مقالتهم بكلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal rejects their claim and supplies the understood subject, the angels: they are honored servants, favored by God and brought near, not offspring.
rows.anchor: أعقب حرف الإضراب عن قولهم بالإخبار بأنهم عباد دون ذكر المبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Initial ḥattā need not mark a regular temporal endpoint; with an independent clause it links statements and marks the speaker’s progression to a new purpose, as in Labīd’s Muʿallaqah.
rows.anchor: فأما ( حتى ) الابتدائية فإن وجود معنى الغاية معها في مواقعها غير منضبط ولا مطرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The use of ḥattā in 2:214 likewise introduces what arose from the distress, not a literal endpoint at which the Messenger spoke.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى : { وزلزلوا حتى يقول الرسول والذين آمنوا معه متى نصر الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene follows the opening of Gog and Magog and the nearness of the promise to convey how quickly the disbelievers’ shock arrives.
rows.anchor: وقد مثلت حالة الكافرين في ذلك الحين بأبلغ تمثيل وأشده وقعا في نفس السامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa and idhā convey sudden, immediate arrival without interval; the pronoun of the story gives a vague advance notice that the following words resolve.
rows.anchor: ثم بتصدير الجملة بحرف المفاجأة والمجازاة الذي يفيد الحصول دفعة بلا تدرج ولا مهلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shukhūṣ is a fixed, unmoving stare, as when someone is stunned.
rows.anchor: والشخوص : إحداد البصر دون تحرك كما يقع للمبهوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is quoted speech with an omitted verb: they say, Woe to us, at that moment.
rows.anchor: مقول قول محذوف كما هو ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī depicts heedlessness as enveloping them like a container surrounds its contents; it is heedlessness toward evidence for resurrection and recompense.
rows.anchor: على تمكن الغفلة منهم حتى كأنها محيطة بهم إحاطة الظرف بالمظروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their cry is a self-directed imprecation prompted by the calamity that has overtaken them.
rows.anchor: دعاء على أنفسهم من شدة ما لحقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal retracts the claim of heedlessness: they had been warned, but wronged themselves through stubborn opposition and turning away.
rows.anchor: للإضراب الإبطالي ، أي ما كنا في غفلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This refers collectively to the events of resurrection, reckoning, and recompense.
rows.anchor: هو مجموع تلك الأحوال من الحشر والحساب والجزاء
